dossiers.catalyst_stack: On 2026-07-02 the EU Court of Justice definitively upheld the €4.1B Android antitrust fine, and on 2026-07-16 the Commission issued binding DMA measures forcing Android AI interoperability and Search data sharing — both directly targeting Google's core distribution moats. On 2026-10-13 a securities fraud class action tied to Gemini 3.5 Pro disclosure issues compounded the legal overhang and explains the 4.4% July share drop. On 2026-06-02/2026-08-27 Alphabet's shift from buybacks to an $85B stock offering adds dilution pressure amid rising AI capex. The lone offset is the 2026-08-28 Q2 earnings beat with Cloud up 82%, but Gemini 4's failure to lift the stock (2026-10-05) suggests waning AI-narrative momentum ahead of Q3 earnings.
dossiers.key_assumption: The EU DMA specification measures and upheld Android fine represent durable structural constraints on Search/Android economics, and litigation risk (class action + private damages suits) keeps a persistent discount on the stock despite strong Cloud growth.

dossiers.catalyst_stack: On 2026-04-29 and 2026-07-22 Alphabet delivered consecutive earnings beats (Q1 blowout; Q2 beat despite a capex surge that pressured shares), establishing fundamental momentum. On 2026-09-02 the ad tech antitrust ruling avoided a breakup — the single most significant positive, removing a binary structural overhang — followed immediately by the 2026-09-03 Gemini 3.8 Flash launch to rebuild AI narrative momentum. On 2026-08-19 the Marvell custom AI chip deal (with an option on a $12.2B stake) deepened the in-house silicon strategy. On 2026-10-13 Alphabet simultaneously faces renewed EU regulatory pressure on Android AI/search data sharing and a securities class action (deadline 2026-12-01), while Wells Fargo's 2026-10-06 PT raise to $417 supports valuation.
dossiers.key_assumption: The favorable September 2 ad tech ruling signals a broader regulatory de-risking (appellate relief on search remedies), and the elevated AI capex will translate into Cloud/TPU revenue growth rather than margin erosion.
